pages.text: Nono opened his window. Snow had fallen overnight—the last snow of winter.
He wanted a big snowman. He rolled a snowball in the yard.
The snowball grew as tall as Nono.
Sparrows flocked to the alley. Nono flew over to watch.
In the sunshine, drops fell from the snowball.
When Nono returned, half of it had melted. It was tiny.
There was little snow left. None to roll into another big ball.
Grandpa Badger pointed to the shaded ground at the bottom of the wall.
White snow lay there. Nono rolled and rolled without stopping.
The biggest snowman stood in the middle of the yard. Nono wrapped his green scarf around its neck.
